headline: Police Association defends IGP's 'crossfire' remarks as timely call
summary: The Bangladesh Police Service Association backs Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir's statement on the use of force if authorized by the government.
details: The Bangladesh Police Service Association has defended Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir's remarks that police would not hesitate to carry out "crossfire" operations if the government authorised them.
The association described the comments as a timely call for enforcing the law firmly while remaining within legal boundaries to strengthen police officers' professional confidence.
IGP Fakir made the remarks on Monday during an event in Dhaka's Chawkbazar, stating that police would act in accordance with the law and the constitution wherever necessary.
He further criticized contradictory public expectations, noting that officers are often labeled authoritarian when using force and weak when they remain restrained.
The Police Service Association added that hesitation in exercising lawful powers could encourage criminals and undermine public safety.
However, the Home Minister and Adviser Zahed Khan have distanced the government from these remarks, stating that there is zero tolerance for extrajudicial killings.
The BNP has also criticized the IGP's comments, with spokesperson Rizvi Hassan calling them embarrassing for the government.
The government has indicated that a final decision regarding the IGP's fate will be made after the Prime Minister returns home.
caption:

IGP Fakir made the remarks on Monday during an event in Dhaka's Chawkbazar, stating that police would act in accordance with the law and the constitution wherever necessary.

He further criticized contradictory public expectations, noting that officers are often labeled authoritarian when using force and weak when they remain restrained.

The Police Service Association added that hesitation in exercising lawful powers could encourage criminals and undermine public safety.

However, the Home Minister and Adviser Zahed Khan have distanced the government from these remarks, stating that there is zero tolerance for extrajudicial killings.

headline_marked: BNP MP's son [[questioned over JCD leader's killing]] in Natore
headline: BNP MP's son questioned over JCD leader's killing in Natore
summary: Md Nuruzzaman Mintu was picked up by the Detective Branch for questioning after JCD leader Md Shakil Islam died from injuries sustained in a brutal attack.
details: Md Shakil Islam, joint general secretary of the Gurudaspur upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), died on Monday at PG Hospital in Dhaka after 12 days of treatment.
Shakil was attacked by a group of helmet-wearing assailants with sharp weapons in the Chachkoir Bazarpara area on October 14.
Following the incident, Shakil's father filed a case with Gurudaspur Police Station against 8 to 10 unidentified individuals.
The Detective Branch (DB) of police has since picked up Md Nuruzzaman Mintu, son of Natore-4 BNP lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz, for questioning.
Local residents claim the killing may be linked to a long-standing rivalry for political dominance between the lawmaker's two sons.
However, MP Abdul Aziz denied the allegations, describing the dispute as a 'family matter' and suggesting the Awami League might be responsible.
The lawmaker stated he would not seek bail for his son unless his innocence is proven and that he fully cooperated with the police.
The death of the JCD leader sparked protests among local party activists in Gurudaspur, who are demanding exemplary punishment for the killers.
caption:
A BNP MP's son has been picked up for questioning after a JCD leader died from injuries sustained in a brutal attack.

Md Shakil Islam, joint general secretary of the Gurudaspur upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), died on Monday at PG Hospital in Dhaka after 12 days of treatment.

Shakil was attacked by a group of helmet-wearing assailants with sharp weapons in the Chachkoir Bazarpara area on October 14.

Following the incident, Shakil's father filed a case with Gurudaspur Police Station against 8 to 10 unidentified individuals.

The Detective Branch (DB) of police has since picked up Md Nuruzzaman Mintu, son of Natore-4 BNP lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz, for questioning.

Local residents claim the killing may be linked to a long-standing rivalry for political dominance between the lawmaker's two sons.

However, MP Abdul Aziz denied the allegations, describing the dispute as a 'family matter' and suggesting the Awami League might be responsible.

The lawmaker stated he would not seek bail for his son unless his innocence is proven and that he fully cooperated with the police.

The death of the JCD leader sparked protests among local party activists in Gurudaspur, who are demanding exemplary punishment for the killers.
